thread:
anya: CI build -> image push is failing intermittently after I changed the Dockerfile to a new multistage layout. job: https://ci.redwood.example/12345 

ci-bot: build #482 failed on step 'push image' — error: HTTP 412 Precondition Failed (layer upload)

sam: can you paste the push logs? 412 usually means registry saw a mismatch in digest or an incomplete blob from a previous upload.

anya: here's the relevant tail of the job log:
```
2026-03-17T14:12:03Z pushing layer sha256:abcd... to registry.redwood.example/repo/image:tag
Uploading 64.0 MiB/256.0 MiB  25% 
Error: received unexpected status: 412 Precondition Failed
Status code should be 201
FATAL: failed to push image
```

matt: did you change any caching or parallel upload flags in the Dockerfile or CI? Kaniko/kaniko-like runners + concurrent pushes can leave stale incomplete blobs.

anya: only change was splitting the build into two stages and adding a tiny extra layer for config. CI uses our kaniko image with cache enabled (we recently turned on remote cache to speed builds).

lee: sounds like remote cache corruption. Quick checks: 1) try `--no-cache` or disable remote cache for one run; 2) try `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.example/repo/image:tag` to see manifest state; 3) check registry logs for `blob upload` incomplete session. Also, if we rotated registry creds recently, uploads can start then 401/412 mid-upload.

sam: +1 to no-cache rerun. If that works, we know it's cache/partial-blob related. If not, we should bisect by reverting the Dockerfile change.

anya: starting a no-cache rerun now: https://ci.redwood.example/12345/482/retry-no-cache 

ci-bot: rerun #482-no-cache started (agent: kaniko-02). CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/12345/482/no-cache

matt: if the no-cache run succeeds, plan: purge the remote cache entries for this repo and re-enable cache. If it still fails, bisect request: @sam can you help revert in a temporary branch and re-run?

sam: yep I can do the bisect if needed. I’ll wait for no-cache result. Also adding a quick local repro command you can run, @anya:
```
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --push --no-cache -t staging.registry/repo/image:localtest .
skopeo copy docker://staging.registry/repo/image:localtest docker://registry.redwood.example/repo/image:stagingtest --dest-tls-verify=false
```

anya: no-cache run just finished — still failing with same 412 on push. 

lee: ok that narrows it: not build cache. Next suspect: registry partial blob state or auth token expiry mid-upload. @eng-infra, any recent registry upgrades or credential rotations?

matt: we rotated the registry service account tokens last night (partial rollout). Ops, could be related. @infra-sre maybe we got some agents hitting old tokens.

ci-bot: alert: registry.redwood.example reported increased 4xx on blob uploads between 2026-03-17T02:30Z-03:15Z. See logs: https://logs.redwood.example/registry/2026-03-17

sam: actionable steps: 1) try a push with smaller chunking (client-side) or single-threaded upload; 2) try pushing to a staging repo then tag/manifest copy server-side; 3) ask registry SRE to list incomplete blob sessions and expire them.

anya: I can try a single-threaded push locally. Running `docker push` from my laptop now (no buildkit).

anya: local docker push succeeded to staging.registry, but pushing to main registry still fails with 412. I ran `skopeo inspect` and got odd manifest partial results.

lee: SRE action: I checked registry, there were orphaned multipart uploads for that repo. I manually expired them and cleared temp blobs for `repo/image`. Trying a small test push now.

ci-bot: registry cleanup job completed for repo/image (expired 7 orphan uploads).

matt: nice. @anya can you re-run the CI push or we can trigger a manual push from your branch?

anya: kicked a CI rebuild (no-cache + fresh agent) — https://ci.redwood.example/12345/482/retry-2

ci-bot: rerun #482-retry-2 started (agent: kaniko-05).

anya: ✅ push succeeded on retry. Looks like orphaned uploads/registry state was the root cause. Thanks @lee and infra-sre for the cleanup.

sam: great — follow-ups: add a short CI healthcheck step to detect 4xx during blob upload and auto-retry or fail fast with a hint to clear registry multipart uploads. Also add a comms note when we rotate registry tokens so people can expect transient pushes to fail.

matt: agreed. Filing a tiny project ticket to add retry+diagnostics to our push step and a runbook for SRE cleanup. I'll ping infra-sre about a faster token-rotation rollout next time. :thumbsup:
